policy: Report an ambiguity and skip only the affected output; never choose a representative description or cluster silently.

questions.question: When the same twelve-level pattern is generated by descriptions with different relative activity classes, which class, or what explicitly defined multiple-class treatment, belongs to that distinct-pattern unit?
affected_outputs: distinct-pattern summaries by relative activity class

questions.question: When the same twelve-level pattern is generated by descriptions in different automaton classes, which automaton class is its bootstrap and logistic cluster?

When descriptions of the same distinct pattern disagree on s = 1, single-placement, or first-letter-settled flags, does the unit count as settled, unsettled, both, or according to a specified description?
When descriptions of the same distinct pattern fall on opposite sides of s >= 2 or s >= 3, how is that pattern's membership in the conditional distinct-pattern census defined?
affected_outputs: the affected conditional distinct-pattern fate shares

questions.question: When descriptions of the same distinct pattern have different letter activity classes, which letter class belongs to the unit in the secondary summaries?

When separate descriptions of the same twelve-level pattern yield different budgeted solver verdicts or fates, may the decided verdict from one description resolve another description's undecided verdict, or must a prescribed common solve be used?
affected_outputs: fate cells for affected distinct patterns

questions.question: P1 literally requires every single-distinct-placement or first-letter-settled description to be F3, while F0 is separately assigned to descriptions with no knots. How should P1 classify such a description that is F0, including the s = 1 cases?
affected_outputs: the interpretation of a literal P1/F0 failure
questions.note: Do not change F0, silently exempt a case, or claim this inconsistency was fixed.

questions.question: For the weighted W secondary comparison, do the 30-decided-unit and under-10%-FU eligibility thresholds use distinct patterns or fair-coin draws, and how should a pattern represented in several automaton classes contribute to the five-cluster threshold?
affected_outputs: W eligibility when these readings do not agree

questions.question: What response or inclusion rule should the logistic sensitivity fit use for FU units: count them as dead, count them as alive, fit both, or exclude them? The two-assignment rule is explicit for matched-cell verdicts but not for this fit.
affected_outputs: a logistic fit containing FU units; its design matrix remains available
